note: A.6 data-quality note: OECD Family Database PF1.1 ('Public spending on family benefits', % of GDP) and PF1.4 ('Tax neutrality of family policies') do NOT publish household gross income by presence of children, contrary to the task brief's assumption. Gross/net income by kids status is instead folded in per-country from the same national household budget/income survey used for A.5 (see each country's 'income_source' field below). Where no clean with/without-kids income split is published by the national survey, income is approximated via decile/quintile position and flagged 'Tier C' or 'N/A'.

US.source: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey (CES) 2024, by household type
US.income_source: BLS CES 2024 (same survey; income before tax reported per consumer unit type)

no_kids.note: necessity_share p50 computed directly from BLS CES 'couple_no_kids' consumer-unit type mean; p90/p99 extrapolated by applying the US CES national necessity-share-by-decile curve's own p50->p90->p99 ratio to this group's mean share (Engel's-law decline in necessity share as income rises), per V4_1_BUILD_SPEC.md instruction to extrapolate from decile data when direct percentile detail isn't published.

with_kids.note: with_kids = weighted average of BLS CES 'with_kids_under6' and 'with_kids_6to17' consumer-unit types, weighted by n_consumer_units_thousands. p90/p99 extrapolated via the same US CES decile-curve ratio technique as no_kids.

DE.source: Statistisches Bundesamt (Destatis), Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe (EVS) 2023, by household type (via BMBF/BPB Sozialbericht 2024 summary tables)

no_kids.note: 'Haushalte ohne Kind' (income; annual EUR) matched with 'Paare ohne Kind' (expenditure; monthly EUR, x12 for annual) -- these are closely-related but not identical household-type definitions (income group includes all no-kids households incl. singles/3+ adults; expenditure group is couples-only). Full EVS category-level expenditure breakdown for these exact groups not extracted (source table gives only total monthly consumption expenditure by household type); necessity_share requires the category breakdown, which was not available within this session's source coverage -- flagged as gap, see README.

with_kids.note: 'Haushalte mit Kind(ern)' (income) matched with 'Paare mit Kind(ern)' (expenditure, monthly EUR x12). Same category-breakdown gap as no_kids.

UK.source: ONS Living Costs and Food Survey (LCF) via Family Spending, detailed household expenditure by household composition, UK, FYE 2024
UK.income_source: N/A - ONS LCF household-composition breakdown tables used here do not publish income (before/after tax) cross-tabulated by household composition at this granularity; income fields are null in the underlying uk_lcf_by_hhtype.json source file

no_kids.note: group = 'nonretired_two_adults' (proxy for couple, no kids). Income not available in source (see income_source note).

with_kids.note: with_kids = weighted average of 'one_or_two_adults_with_one_child' and 'one_or_two_adults_with_two_or_more_children' groups, weighted by weighted_households_thousands. Income not available in source.

JP.source: MHLW Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions (Kokumin Seikatsu Kiso Chosa) 2023 income year, Table 38, nuclear-family household income by structure; expenditure interpolated from Statistics Bureau Family Income and Expenditure Survey (FIES) 2024 by-decile curve at the matching income level
JP.income_source: MHLW Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions 2023, Table 38 (via e-Stat/ecitizen.jp mirror of official table): 核家族世帯_夫婦のみの世帯 (couple only) = ¥5,241,000; 核家族世帯_夫婦と未婚の子のみの世帯 (couple + unmarried children only) = ¥8,239,000

no_kids.note: income is Tier A/direct (MHLW national survey, couple-only nuclear household). Expenditure is Tier B: not a direct kids-split FIES figure -- interpolated from the FIES 2024 by-decile income/expenditure curve at the income level matching this group's income (¥5,241,000, close to FIES d4-d5).

with_kids.note: income is Tier A/direct (MHLW national survey, couple + unmarried children nuclear household). Expenditure interpolated from FIES 2024 by-decile curve at ¥8,239,000 (close to FIES d7-d8), same caveat as no_kids.

CH.source: Modeled: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) Household Budget Survey (HABE) 2023 quintile income/expenditure curve (ch_habe.json) x kids-income-uplift ratio averaged from DE (Destatis EVS 2023) and JP (MHLW 2023) with/without-kids gross-income ratios
CH.income_source: Modeled -- BFS HABE standard tables [31-33] 'couples without children' and [41-43] 'couples with children' exist per BFS HBS methodology documentation (https://dam-api.bfs.admin.ch/hub/api/dam/assets/29805023/master) but rendered numeric tables were not retrievable within this session's time budget; documented as a Tier 3 gap and modeled instead
CH.modeled_from: DE+JP kids-income-ratio applied to CH's own quintile curve

no_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C) -- see country-level source note. Not a direct BFS with/without-kids figure.

with_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C) -- see country-level source note. Not a direct BFS with/without-kids figure.

FI.source: Modeled: Statistics Finland Household Budget Survey (HBS) quintile income/expenditure curve (fi_hbs.json) x kids-income-uplift ratio averaged from DE and JP with/without-kids gross-income ratios
FI.income_source: Modeled -- StatFin table 12ec ('Households' income by number of adults and children, 1987-2023') is the ideal direct source but its PxWeb query-builder page could not be extracted as numeric values via fetch_url within this session's time budget (needs a PxWeb JSON-stat API call, not completed); documented as a Tier 3 gap and modeled instead
FI.modeled_from: DE+JP kids-income-ratio applied to FI's own quintile curve

no_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C) -- see country-level source note. Not a direct StatFin with/without-kids figure. Income basis is after-tax (fi_hbs.json only has avg_income_after_tax, not before_tax).

with_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C) -- see country-level source note. Same after-tax income basis caveat as no_kids.

NO.source: Modeled: NO income/expenditure decile (v3 peer-modeled from FI, no_expenditure_modeled.json / se_expenditure_modeled.json, d5 anchor) x Finland with_kids/no_kids ratios (income, expenditure, necessity_share) derived in this file
NO.income_source: Modeled -- no direct NO national household-income-by-kids-status source found; OECD Family Database PF1.1/PF1.4 do not publish this indicator (see top-level note). Peer-modeled from Finland per V4_1_BUILD_SPEC.md instruction.

no_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C), peer-modeled from Finland's with_kids/no_kids ratio applied to NO's own d5 (median decile) income and expenditure from the v3 peer-modeled file.

with_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C), same peer-modeling approach as no_kids.

SE.source: Modeled: SE income/expenditure decile (v3 peer-modeled from FI, no_expenditure_modeled.json / se_expenditure_modeled.json, d5 anchor) x Finland with_kids/no_kids ratios (income, expenditure, necessity_share) derived in this file
SE.income_source: Modeled -- no direct SE national household-income-by-kids-status source found; OECD Family Database PF1.1/PF1.4 do not publish this indicator (see top-level note). Peer-modeled from Finland per V4_1_BUILD_SPEC.md instruction.

no_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C), peer-modeled from Finland's with_kids/no_kids ratio applied to SE's own d5 (median decile) income and expenditure from the v3 peer-modeled file.

with_kids.note: Modeled (Tier C), same peer-modeling approach as no_kids.
